{{Short description|Theorem about seven tangent circles}}
[[File:Teorema de les set circumferències.svg|250px|thumb|Seven circles theorem]]In [[geometry]], the '''seven circles theorem''' is a theorem about a certain arrangement of seven [[circle]]s in the [[Euclidean plane]].  Specifically, given a chain of six circles all [[tangent]] to a seventh circle and each tangent to its two neighbors, the three [[Line (geometry)|lines]] drawn between opposite pairs of the points of tangency on the seventh circle all pass through the same [[Point (geometry)|point]].  Though elementary in nature, this theorem was not discovered until 1974 (by Evelyn, Money-Coutts, and Tyrrell).
